faqs.q: How much does a Cane Corso cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Cane Corso puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Cane Corso, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Cane Corso cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Cane Corso are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Cane Corsos shed a lot?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Cane Corso need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Cane Corso's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Cane Corsos that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Cane Corsos easy to train?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Cane Corsos. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Most Cane Corsos learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Cane Corsos commonly have?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos are most commonly associated with bloat (GDV). Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Cane Corsos live?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos have an average lifespan of 9–12 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Cane Corsos prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Cane Corso puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Cane Corso puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Cane Corso-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Cane Corsos good with kids?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Cane Corsos get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Cane Corsos bark a lot?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Cane Corsos good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Cane Corso need per day?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Cane Corsos good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Cane Corsos make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Cane Corso doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Cane Corsos often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Cane Corso be off-lead?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Cane Corso?
faqs.a: A Cane Corso needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Adult Cane Corsos should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Cane Corsos benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Cane Corso from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Cane Corsos can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Cane Corso a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Cane Corsos good family dogs?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Cane Corsos do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Cane Corsos form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Cane Corso?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Cane Corso — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
